main_text.head: Cap. 17. De Interrogatione.
main_text.p: Interrogando plurima addiscere poterit studiosus, si modò rectè interroget. Rectè autem interrogabit, si hos canones observabit.
1. Interrogatio sit brevis, aptè formata ad scopum, & crebra.
2. Fiat coràm, vivâ voce, & per literas.
3. Interrogentur ii, qui eruditi, qui non invidi, qui nobis deniq; favent.
main_text.head: Cap. 18. De Examine.
main_text.p: Examen est eorum, quæ meminisse volumus, repetitio. De eâ notentur hi canones.
1. Repetitio prima sit solitaria, & tacita, & curforia, quâ celerius colliguntur audita & scripta.
2. Sequatur sociata, cùm duo per vices repetitionem instituunt: sic, ut unus prælegat dictata, alter audiat.
3. Addatur tarda & fixa seu Pythagorea repetitio: quæ semper sit gemina. Prior serviat intelle-ctui, ut intelligas rem: posterior serviat memoriæ, ut intellecta imprimas & serves.
4. Examen sit diurnum, hebdomadarium, menstruum, bimestre, trimestre, semestre, & deniq; annuum.

page.notes: The first word of the third group is printed "Exæmen" with the æ at the edge of the scan; the ending of "est" is partly cut off, so the final letter is doubtful. The lines are set in a narrow column with wide spacing between the numbered items. Printed "deniq;" is split at the line end as "de-" / "niq;" with the mark after "niq" partly unclear (possibly a superscript 3 standing for ";"). The left-margin marks beside "Examen" and "curforia" are not printed text and were left out. The large initials E and I are joined to their words.
